### Key takeaways
- Our gap map shows audits far outnumber outcome trials: 5,012 of 6,332 AI papers from 2022–2026 address fairness, but only 35 are RCTs.
- LLM bias has now been shown on real ED records ([UTSW](https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/newsroom/articles/year-2026/oct-ai-enabled-triage-tools-human-biases.html)) and in a deployed scribe ([medRxiv](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.14.26360467v1.full)), not only in vignettes.
- HHS's June vacatur dropped only gender-identity provisions ([NFP](https://www.nfp.com/insights/hhs-vacates-rule-prohibiting-gender-identity-discrimination/)). The 2024 rule's decision-tool duty still applies ([Crowell](https://www.crowell.com/en/insights/client-alerts/hhs-applies-discrimination-prohibitions-to-use-of-automated-and-non-automated-patient-care-decision-support-tools)).

### What's new
- **Oct 29** — Cedars-Sinai's Tiffani Bright: hospitals can't inspect vendor "black box" training data, and overall accuracy can hide subgroup failures ([AHCJ](https://healthjournalism.org/blog/2026/10/black-box-medical-ai-can-deepen-health-disparities-researcher-says)).
- **Oct 20** — Three open LLMs triaged Stanford and BIDMC ED records. Stigmatizing wording wrongly downgraded nearly 10% of patients in some instances ([UTSW](https://www.utsouthwestern.edu/newsroom/articles/year-2026/oct-ai-enabled-triage-tools-human-biases.html)).
- **Sep 21** — WHO flags bias as a risk that current ethics review may miss and calls for local LMIC research leadership ([WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/21-09-2026-new-who-report-calls-for-stronger-ethics-oversight-of-ai-related-health-research)).
- **Aug 17** — Across 54,160 safety-net visits, Spanish, Portuguese and Haitian Creole encounters had lower odds (OR 0.75–0.79) of mostly unedited Abridge notes ([medRxiv](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.14.26360467v1.full)).

### Novel gaps
1. **Trials of debiased models.** Evidence: 2 RCTs among 555 mitigation papers; NYC H+H threshold fix was retrospective ([npj](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-025-01732-w)). Study: stepped-wedge RCT, safety-net EHRs; endpoint: racial gap in missed deterioration. Funder: AHRQ/PCORI.
2. **Safety of LLM tools by patient language.** Evidence: 5.2% of 657 LLM-bias papers prospective; the scribe study didn't assess accuracy or safety ([medRxiv](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.08.14.26360467v1.full)). Study: prospective multisite note review in interpreter visits; endpoint: harmful errors. Funder: AHRQ.
3. **Post-market subgroup checks of cleared AI devices.** Evidence: FDA summary reporting didn't improve with clearance year (OR 1.02, n=519) ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12360)). Study: multisite registry comparing device output with ground truth by race, sex and age. Funder: FDA CDRH.

*Dropped because recent work covers them: race-free eGFR outcomes ([JAMA IM via Healio](https://www.healio.com/news/nephrology/20260429/waittime-policy-tied-to-increased-kidney-transplant-rates-for-black-candidates)) and neonatal oximetry bias (NeoPODS, prospective, [Masimo release](https://www.masimo.com/media/masimo-set-r-pulse-oximetry-performed-accurately-on-hospitalized-newborns-of-all-skin-tones-in-largest-ever-prospective-real-world-study)).*

### Outlook
The research is shifting from vignette audits to tools already in use, and WHO now asks funders, journals and regulators to deal with systemic AI risks that single-project ethics review can't catch ([WHO](https://www.who.int/news/item/21-09-2026-new-who-report-calls-for-stronger-ethics-oversight-of-ai-related-health-research)).
